oneOf.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp, the record's own event time.

The key of a record of another type. A reference keeps the target
type's own key; it is never prefixed with a device.

description.description:
What the field holds, in the operator's words: its meaning, its unit,
an example ("Estimated cost of the session in US dollars, e.g. 0.42").
Wild carries it onto the table's field. Optional; at most 280
characters.

KeyClass.description: How a shape's records get their ids.

oneOf.description:
The id is the shape's declared key fields: a re-read writes nothing
new, and a record changed under its id is refused
(`source_rewrote_history`).

The id is an append-only file's generation and byte offset, in the
reserved fields `_generation` (text) and `_offset` (a whole number); a
restored file's line is re-keyed by Wild (`generation_reassigned`).

The id is a per-install epoch and counter, in the reserved fields
`_epoch` and `_seq` (a whole number), for events seen only in the
moment; never backfilled.

ShapeDecl.description:
A declared shape: its version, its key class, its fields and the type its
records are proposed to fill.

description.description:
What one record of this shape is, in the operator's words ("One
finished work session in OpenCode"). Optional; at most 280 characters.

key.description:
The fields that form a `natural` key. Empty for a `position` or a
`live` shape, which carry their key parts in reserved fields.

target_type.description:
The type the producer proposes this shape fills, usually a new one of
its own. The operator accepts it or maps the shape into another type.

SourceDecl.description: One source a producer feeds: a slug and the shapes it sends.

description.description:
What the source is, in the operator's words ("Usage of the OpenCode
agent on this machine"). Optional; at most 280 characters.

ToolActs.description: What a tool does when it is called.

oneOf.description: It only reads: nothing changes anywhere.

It changes or starts something outside Wild: writes a document,
starts an agent.

A word this contract does not know — `writes` among them: a
connector's call changes nothing inside Wild (its records come over
the data road), so `writes` is not a connector's word. Refused.

acts.description:
`reads`, or `outward` for anything it changes or starts. Required:
the door refuses a tool that does not say.

description.description:
What it does, in the operator's words ("Starts an agent on this
host"). The operator reads it on the card before the yes. At most 280
characters.

name.description:
The function's name, the same on every device of the connector
(`agent_start`): lowercase letters, digits and `_`, at most 64.

risk.description:
How risky a call is: `low`, `medium` or `high`. Absent, Wild takes
the lowest it allows for what the tool acts on.

routes_by.description:
The argument whose value names the device that answers a call, when
several devices offer it (normally `host`). One of the schema's
properties.

schema.description:
The JSON Schema of its arguments: an object whose `properties`
include `idempotency_key`, using only the keywords Wild checks
and annotations whose key starts with `x-`.

ToolRisk.description: How much harm a call could do if it went wrong.

oneOf.description: A word this contract does not know. Refused.

answers_for.description:
The values this device answers for: the values a call
may name in a tool's `routes_by` argument to reach this device,
normally this host's name. A call is routed by the calling tribe and
this value together, never by value alone. Empty: the device claims
no value — a device that offers no tool claims none, and so may not
declare any.

contract_version.description: The contract version it was built against.

fingerprint.description:
The machine fingerprint: an app-specific HMAC of the machine's stable
identifier. Only a hint for offering continuation, never an identity.

needs_vocabulary.description: Whether it needs the vocabulary of project and customer names.

references.description:
Existing types of the tribe the producer's shapes reference. It never
writes into them.

tools.description: The functions it offers Wild to call once the operator said yes. A connector that only sends announces none.

tribe.description: The tribe it proposes, if any. Absent, Wild proposes one.
